verdict: RIGID FIT INFEASIBLE within anatomical tolerances. Two runs: (1) with soft containment the optimiser buried 24% of the muscle through the wall to close the base gap (rotation 46.7 deg) -- rejected, cost re-specified; (2) with near-hard containment and a 15-deg refinement bound, the optimum violates every gate slightly and simultaneously (base gap 2.24 mm, tips 40.3 mm, rotation 17.0 deg, full-res inside 0.943/0.919). Simultaneous marginal violation of independent constraints is the signature of joint infeasibility, not of a local minimum.
root_cause_hypothesis: Upstream segmentation. papillary_muscles.stl is 50 disconnected fragments spanning 84 mm (a real PM pair spans ~40-50 mm); the k-means split into anterolateral/posteromedial inherits that. The pair's mutual pose is therefore not trustworthy, so registering them as one rigid body imposes a wrong constraint, and registering them separately would be fitting noise.
recommended_next: Re-derive the papillary muscles from LV_myocardium_frameA.stl (Claude Code's mirrored, validated myocardium, already in frame A): the myocardium regions that protrude inside the blood-pool convex hull ARE the PMs and trabeculae. That uses data already in the correct frame and needs no registration.
